Feature: Register Default Value and Write/Read Verification
Test Description: This test case verifies the register accessibility and data integrity of 434 registers across the DWC Ethernet QoS IP (ethernet1). The test validates two fundamental aspects of register behavior: (1) that all registers hold their expected default (reset) values after power-on, and (2) that writable register fields correctly accept, store, and return written data patterns while read-only fields retain their default values. The test covers registers spanning the MAC, MMC, MTL (including per-queue registers for queues 0-3), and DMA (including per-channel registers for channels 0-3) functional blocks. Registers are selectively skipped based on predefined skip arrays for both default value checking and write/read checking phases. The test uses read masks and write masks to account for read-only, write-only, and reserved bit fields within each register.
Test Steps / Procedure:
Phase 1 - Default Value Verification:
1. Iterate through all 434 registers in the register address array.
2. For each register, check if the register is readable (non-zero read mask). Skip non-readable registers.
3. Check if the register is marked for skipping in the reset-skip array. Skip if flagged.
4. Read the current value of the register.
5. Compare the read value against the expected default value from the default value array.
6. If mismatch, increment the default-fail counter and log the failure with register identity, expected value, and actual read value.

Phase 2 - Write/Read Pattern Verification:
7. For each of 6 data patterns (all-ones, alternating-AA, alternating-55, all-zeros, alternating-A5, upper-half-ones), perform steps 8-13.
8. Write Phase: Iterate through all 434 registers. Skip registers flagged in the skip array. Skip registers with zero write mask (non-writable). Write the current data pattern to each eligible register.
9. Read Phase: Iterate through all 434 registers. Skip registers flagged in the skip array. Skip registers with zero write mask. Skip registers with zero read mask (non-readable).
10. Read the current value of each eligible register.
11. Compute the expected value by combining the written data pattern (masked by both read mask and write mask) with the default value for read-only bits (masked by the inverted write mask and read mask).
12. Compare the read value against the computed expected value.
13. If mismatch, increment the write-fail counter and log the failure with register identity, expected value, and actual read value.

Phase 3 - Final Verdict:
14. If either the default-fail counter or write-fail counter is greater than zero, signal test failure.
15. Otherwise, signal test success.

Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
1. Default Value Check: Every readable register (not flagged for skip in the reset-skip array) must return its documented default value when read after power-on reset. Any mismatch between the read value and the expected default value constitutes a failure, and the default-fail counter is incremented.

2. Write/Read Pattern Check: For each of the 6 test data patterns, every writable and readable register (not flagged for skip in the skip array) must return the expected value after a write operation. The expected value is computed as: writable bits reflect the written pattern (masked by both write mask and read mask), while non-writable bits retain their default values (masked by inverted write mask and read mask). Any mismatch between the read value and the computed expected value constitutes a failure, and the write-fail counter is incremented.

3. Overall Pass/Fail: The test passes (finish with success) if and only if both the default-fail counter and the write-fail counter remain at zero after all phases complete. If either counter is greater than zero, the test fails (finish with failure).

4. Certain registers are intentionally skipped during the write/read phase via a skip array (e.g., VLAN Tag Control, VLAN Tag Data, and select TX Flow Control registers). Certain registers are also skipped during the default value check phase via a separate reset-skip array. These skips are by design and do not affect the pass/fail verdict.
Remarks: The test covers 434 registers across MAC, MMC, MTL (queues 0-3), and DMA (channels 0-3) blocks of the DWC Ethernet QoS IP. A soft reset check function is defined in the source but is commented out and not executed in the active test flow. The 6 data patterns used for write/read verification provide comprehensive bit-toggling coverage including all-ones, all-zeros, alternating bit patterns, and split-half patterns. Registers with special access behavior (e.g., write-1-to-clear status registers, self-clearing control bits) are handled via the skip array mechanism.

Feature: Basic TX (Transmit) Operation with Interrupt Handling
Test Description: This test case verifies the basic transmit (TX) operation of the DWC Ethernet QoS IP (ethernet1) using DMA channel 0. The test validates the end-to-end TX data path by configuring MAC address registers with DMA channel selection and address enable for 4 MAC addresses, setting up the MAC packet filter for hash filtering and receive-all mode, enabling TX and RX in full duplex mode via the MAC Configuration register, programming all 4 MTL TX queues with store-and-forward mode and queue sizes, configuring quantum weights for TX queue scheduling, enabling RX queue overflow and TX queue underflow interrupts on all 4 MTL queues, configuring the DMA system bus mode for outstanding requests and burst selection, preloading TX descriptors, programming DMA channel TX descriptor ring lengths, list base addresses, and tail pointers for all 4 channels, configuring DMA channel controls, enabling DMA channel interrupts for all 4 channels, and initiating TX on DMA channel 0. The test uses an interrupt-driven polling mechanism where the interrupt handler reads current TX descriptor and buffer pointers for all 4 DMA channels, reads and clears DMA interrupt status by writing to individual DMA channel status registers, and signals completion to the main test loop. The test iterates through 10 interrupt cycles to verify sustained TX operation.
Test Steps / Procedure:
Step 1 - MAC Address Configuration:
1. Configure MAC Address3 High register with address enable, DMA channel 3 selection, and upper MAC address bits.
2. Configure MAC Address2 High register with address enable, DMA channel 2 selection, and upper MAC address bits.
3. Configure MAC Address1 High register with address enable, DMA channel 1 selection, and upper MAC address bits.
4. Configure MAC Address0 High register with address enable, DMA channel 0 selection, and upper MAC address bits.
5. Configure MAC Address3 Low through MAC Address0 Low registers with lower 32-bit MAC address values.

Step 2 - MAC Configuration:
6. Configure MAC Packet Filter register to enable hash filtering and receive-all mode.
7. Configure MAC Configuration register to enable TX and RX with full duplex mode and speed selection.
8. Configure MAC Extended Configuration register with default settings.

Step 3 - MTL TX Queue Configuration:
9. Configure MTL TxQ3 through TxQ0 Operation Mode registers with TX queue size (4096 bytes) and store-and-forward mode.
10. Configure MTL TxQ3 through TxQ0 Quantum Weight registers with scheduling weight values.
11. Configure MTL Q3 through Q0 Interrupt Control Status registers to enable RX queue overflow and TX queue underflow interrupts.

Step 4 - DMA System Bus Configuration:
12. Configure DMA System Bus Mode register for outstanding request limits, fixed burst, address-aligned burst enable, and burst length selection.

Step 5 - TX Descriptor Preload:
13. Preload TX descriptors into memory for DMA channel 0 operation.

Step 6 - DMA Channel TX Descriptor Configuration:
14. Configure DMA CH3 through CH0 TX Descriptor Ring Length registers with the descriptor ring size.
15. Configure DMA CH3 through CH0 TX Descriptor List Address registers with the base address of the first TX descriptor.
16. Configure DMA CH3 through CH0 TX Descriptor Tail Pointer registers to indicate the end of the descriptor ring.
17. Configure DMA CH3 through CH0 Control registers.

Step 7 - DMA Interrupt Enable:
18. Enable DMA channel interrupts for channels 0 through 3 via the DMA CH0-CH3 Interrupt Enable registers.
19. Enable system-level ethernet interrupts.

Step 8 - Start TX:
20. Start TX on DMA channel 0 by writing to the DMA CH0 TX Control register. (TX start for channels 1-3 is not active in this test.)

Step 9 - Interrupt-Driven Polling:
21. Enter a polling loop (10 iterations). In each iteration, wait for the transfer complete interrupt.
22. Upon interrupt, the interrupt handler executes:
    a. Read current TX descriptor pointer and TX buffer pointer for DMA channels 0 through 3.
    b. Read DMA Interrupt Status register to observe aggregate interrupt state.
    c. Clear individual DMA channel status registers (CH0 through CH3) by writing all-ones (write-1-to-clear).
    d. Re-read DMA Interrupt Status register to confirm status is cleared.
    e. Clear system-level interrupt.
    f. Signal interrupt completion to the main polling loop.
23. After 10 interrupt cycles, wait for a settling period.

Step 10 - Test Completion:
24. Signal test success.

Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
1. MAC Address Configuration: MAC Address0 through Address3 High and Low registers must be successfully written with the specified DMA channel selection, address enable, and MAC address values.

2. MAC and MTL Configuration: MAC Configuration register must enable TX and RX in full duplex mode. MAC Packet Filter must enable hash filtering and receive-all mode. All 4 MTL TX queue Operation Mode registers must be configured with the specified queue size and store-and-forward settings. All 4 MTL TX queue Quantum Weight registers must accept the scheduling weight values. All 4 MTL queue Interrupt Control Status registers must enable the specified overflow and underflow interrupts.

3. DMA Configuration: DMA System Bus Mode register must be configured with the specified outstanding request, burst, and alignment settings. All 4 DMA channel TX Descriptor Ring Length, List Address, Tail Pointer, and Control registers must be successfully programmed.

4. DMA Interrupt Enable: All 4 DMA channel Interrupt Enable registers must be configured to enable the specified interrupt sources.

5. TX Operation: After starting TX on DMA channel 0 via the DMA CH0 TX Control register, the DMA engine must process TX descriptors and generate transfer complete interrupts.

6. Interrupt Handling: The interrupt handler must successfully read the current TX descriptor pointer and TX buffer pointer from all 4 DMA channels. The DMA Interrupt Status register must reflect active interrupt status before clearing. After writing all-ones to each DMA channel Status register (write-1-to-clear), the DMA Interrupt Status register must reflect cleared status upon re-read.

7. Interrupt Polling: The test must successfully complete 10 interrupt-driven polling iterations, with each iteration receiving a transfer complete interrupt that clears the pending flag.

8. Test Completion: The test signals success upon completing all 10 interrupt cycles and the settling wait period. No conditional failure path exists in the test; the test always signals success if it reaches completion.
Remarks: TX is started only on DMA channel 0 in this test. TX start for DMA channels 1, 2, and 3 is defined in the source but is inactive (commented out). All 4 DMA channels are configured with descriptor ring lengths, list addresses, tail pointers, controls, and interrupt enables, but only channel 0 actively transmits. The interrupt handler reads TX descriptor and buffer pointers for all 4 channels regardless of active TX status. DMA channel status register reads within the interrupt handler are defined but inactive (commented out) in both the pre-clear and post-clear sections. The test uses a preload descriptor mechanism to set up TX descriptors in memory before starting the DMA engine. System-level interrupt enable and clear operations reference registers outside the DWC Ethernet QoS IP register space.
